assertion_results.text: Epics are generated between Feature and Tasks — at least 2 Epics are created (one per repository) when by-repository grouping is used
assertion_results.evidence: impact-map.md documents 'Grouping strategy: by-repository' and defines two Epics: 'Epic 1: TC-9006: trustify-backend' and 'Epic 2: TC-9006: trustify-ui'. Both are created with 'Issue type: Epic (level-1)' and 'Parent: TC-9006 (Feature)'.

assertion_results.text: Each Epic summary follows the format '<feature-key>: <repository-name>' (e.g., 'TC-9006: trustify-backend', 'TC-9006: trustify-ui')
assertion_results.evidence: impact-map.md shows Epic 1 summary as 'TC-9006: trustify-backend' and Epic 2 summary as 'TC-9006: trustify-ui', both matching the required format exactly.

assertion_results.text: Each task specifies its parent Epic key in the output — tasks targeting trustify-backend are assigned to the backend Epic, tasks targeting trustify-ui are assigned to the frontend Epic
assertion_results.evidence: impact-map.md Task-to-Epic Assignment table maps Tasks 1, 2, 3, 8 (trustify-backend) to Epic 'TC-9006: trustify-backend' and Tasks 4, 5, 6, 7 (trustify-ui) to Epic 'TC-9006: trustify-ui'. Each task's Repository section matches its Epic assignment.

assertion_results.text: The plan documents Incorporates links from the Feature to each Epic (not from Feature to individual Tasks) — evidenced by link decisions in the impact map or task output files
assertion_results.evidence: impact-map.md Issue Links section states: 'Feature TC-9006 → Incorporates → Epic "TC-9006: trustify-backend"' and 'Feature TC-9006 → Incorporates → Epic "TC-9006: trustify-ui"' with explicit note '(Feature links to Epics only, not to individual Tasks. Tasks inherit hierarchy through their Epic parent.)'

assertion_results.text: Task dependency ordering is preserved within and across Epics — backend tasks have lower task numbers than dependent frontend tasks
assertion_results.evidence: Backend tasks are numbered 1, 2, 3 (core implementation). Frontend tasks are numbered 4, 5, 6, 7, all with higher numbers. Task 4 (frontend API client) depends on Task 2 (backend endpoints). Task 5 depends on Task 4. Task 6 depends on Task 5. Task 7 depends on Tasks 5 and 6. Task 8 (documentation) depends on all prior tasks. Dependency ordering is correctly preserved.

assertion_results.text: Each non-documentation, non-testing task file contains all required template sections: Repository, Target Branch, Description, at least one of Files to Modify or Files to Create, Implementation Notes, Acceptance Criteria, Test Requirements. Documentation tasks (tasks whose filename or description indicates doc-only scope) and testing tasks (tasks whose filename or description indicates cross-cutting testing scope) are exempt from requiring Files to Modify, Files to Create, and Implementation Notes — they must still include Repository, Target Branch, Description, Acceptance Criteria, and Test Requirements
assertion_results.evidence: Non-doc/non-test tasks (1, 2, 4, 5, 6) all contain Repository, Target Branch, Description, Files to Create and/or Files to Modify, Implementation Notes, Acceptance Criteria, Test Requirements. Testing tasks (3: 'integration tests', 7: 'frontend tests') contain Repository, Target Branch, Description, Acceptance Criteria, Test Requirements (plus optional Files to Create/Modify and Implementation Notes). Documentation task (8: 'Document remediation dashboard') contains Repository, Target Branch, Description, Acceptance Criteria, Test Requirements. All required sections present for each task type.

assertion_results.text: The plan documents Epic creation with the level-1 issue type name ('Epic') and parent set to the feature issue key — evidenced by Epic creation parameters in the impact map or output files
assertion_results.evidence: impact-map.md explicitly states for both Epics: 'Issue type: Epic (level-1)' and 'Parent: TC-9006 (Feature)'. summary-comment.md confirms: 'Epic: TC-9006: trustify-backend (issue type: Epic, parent: TC-9006)' and 'Epic: TC-9006: trustify-ui (issue type: Epic, parent: TC-9006)'.

assertion_results.text: Every generated task description contains a Repository section with a single repository name (not multiple repos per task)
assertion_results.evidence: All 8 task files contain a '## Repository' section with a single repository name: Tasks 1, 2, 3, 8 have 'trustify-backend'; Tasks 4, 5, 6, 7 have 'trustify-ui'. No task lists multiple repositories.

assertion_results.text: Every generated task description contains Target Branch, Description, Acceptance Criteria, and Test Requirements sections as required by the handoff contract in task-description-template.md
assertion_results.evidence: All 8 task files contain '## Target Branch' (all set to 'main'), '## Description', '## Acceptance Criteria' (with checkbox items), and '## Test Requirements' (with checkbox items).

assertion_results.text: For each task created, a description digest is produced — evidenced by a separate digest file (e.g., task-N-digest.md), a digest entry in the impact map, or a '[sdlc-workflow] Description digest: sha256-md:<64-char-hex>' marker in any output file. The digest must contain a format-tagged SHA-256 hash — exactly 64 lowercase hex characters prefixed by 'sha256-md:' or 'sha256-adf:'
assertion_results.evidence: Eight separate digest files exist (task-1-digest.md through task-8-digest.md). Each contains '[sdlc-workflow] Description digest: sha256-md:<64-hex-chars>'. Example: task-1-digest.md contains 'sha256-md:286bb74175212b4690fdd549eba872c929aa32026151384d3045fc4070d6fc1a' (64 lowercase hex characters with sha256-md: prefix).

assertion_results.text: Convention-aware enrichment validates file-type applicability per shared/convention-applicability-rules.md before including a convention — inapplicable conventions are excluded entirely (not listed with 'Not applicable' annotations), and applicable ones include a rationale in the prescribed format ('Applies: task modifies <file> matching the convention's <scope>'), not free-form prose
assertion_results.evidence: All convention annotations in task files use the prescribed format. Examples: Task 1: 'Applies: task creates modules/fundamental/src/remediation/service/remediation.rs matching the convention's .rs file scope.' Task 4: 'Applies: task modifies src/api/rest.ts matching the convention's .ts file scope.' Task 5: 'Applies: task modifies src/routes.tsx matching the convention's .tsx file scope.' No inapplicable conventions are listed with 'Not applicable' or similar annotations — only applicable conventions appear with proper rationale.

assertion_results.text: When the Feature issue has a priority set (not 'Undefined'), the plan documents that the Feature's priority is inherited by created tasks — evidenced by priority field values in the impact map, task creation log, or task description files. When the Feature's priority is 'Undefined', the plan documents that priority inheritance is skipped (not propagated as null or 'Undefined')
assertion_results.evidence: Feature TC-9006 has priority 'Major'. impact-map.md documents: 'priority: propagated from Feature TC-9006 (Major)' in the Task additional_fields section, and the Inherited Field Values section states 'Priority: Major (inherited from Feature TC-9006, propagated to all Epics and Tasks)'. Epic definitions include '"priority": {"name": "Major"}'. summary-comment.md confirms: 'Priority: Major — propagated from Feature TC-9006 to all Epics and Tasks'.

assertion_results.text: When the Feature issue has a non-empty fixVersions array and the fixVersion scope config (from ### Jira Field Defaults in CLAUDE.md) is 'task' or 'both' (or absent, defaulting to 'both'), the plan documents that fixVersions are inherited by created tasks — evidenced by fixVersion values in the impact map, task creation log, or task description files. When fixVersion scope is 'feature' or the Feature has no fixVersions, the plan documents that fixVersion inheritance is skipped
assertion_results.evidence: Feature TC-9006 has fixVersions: ['RHTPA 1.5.0']. CLAUDE.md specifies 'fixVersion scope: both'. impact-map.md documents: 'fixVersions: propagated from Feature TC-9006 (RHTPA 1.5.0); fixVersion scope is "both" per Jira Field Defaults, so propagation is active'. Task additional_fields include '"fixVersions": [{"name": "RHTPA 1.5.0"}]'. Epic definitions also include fixVersions. summary-comment.md confirms: 'Fix Versions: RHTPA 1.5.0 — propagated from Feature TC-9006 to all Epics and Tasks (fixVersion scope: "both")'.

assertion_results.text: A summary of inherited field propagation is produced — evidenced by a summary-comment.md file in the outputs directory, or a summary section in the impact map that includes the inherited priority and fixVersion values propagated to tasks, or states they were omitted and why
assertion_results.evidence: summary-comment.md exists in the outputs directory and contains an 'Inherited Field Values' section: 'Priority: Major — propagated from Feature TC-9006 to all Epics and Tasks' and 'Fix Versions: RHTPA 1.5.0 — propagated from Feature TC-9006 to all Epics and Tasks (fixVersion scope: "both")'. The impact-map.md also contains a matching 'Inherited Field Values' section.
